title: SpaceX Catches a Returning Starship Spacecraft for the First Time, Tesla Opens $299/Month Cybercab Pre-Orders, and FAA Traces Its Outage to an L3Harris Upgrade
subhead: SpaceX achieved a historic aerospace milestone in South Texas by catching an orbital-class Starship upper-stage spacecraft with its launch tower arms after a full day in orbit; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced Friday's four-hour nationwide FAA ground stop was triggered by a contractor upgrade to an L3Harris telecom system and faulty copper wiring; and Elon Musk joined 115,000 signatories petitioning to reinstate ousted chip chief Jensen Huang as Tesla opened $299/month Cybercab pre-orders.

sections.heading: SpaceX Pulls Off First-Ever Launch Tower Catch of a Returning Orbital Starship Spacecraft in South Texas
sections.body:
Ars Technica, The Hill, and Le Monde — SpaceX achieved a landmark aerospace engineering feat on Saturday afternoon at Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas, successfully using giant mechanical 'chopstick' arms on its launch tower to catch the returning upper-stage Starship spacecraft after the vehicle completed a full 24-hour orbital mission on Flight 15 and survived hypersonic atmospheric reentry. SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot hailed the intact orbital spacecraft recovery as 'the Holy Grail of space flight,' demonstrating the rapid full-stage reusability required for NASA's Artemis lunar lander program and high-cadence satellite deployments while drawing rare bipartisan praise from lawmakers in Washington (The Hill, MarketWatch).

In deep-space astronomy, scientists working with the European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope announced the discovery of 31 ancient quasars from the early universe—including two supermassive black hole engines shining with the luminosity of a trillion suns—while observations from the James Webb Space Telescope detected pristine protoplanetary water and carbon dioxide ice older than its host star (Science Daily, Ars Technica).
sections.whyItMatters: Catching a returning orbital Starship upper stage proves SpaceX can recover both halves of the world's largest rocket, slashing orbital launch costs for lunar missions and heavy satellite constellations.

sections.heading: DOT Traces Nationwide FAA Flight Ground Stop to an L3Harris Telecom Upgrade and Faulty Copper Wiring
sections.body:
CNBC, TechCrunch, and The Register — United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced on Saturday that Friday's four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop—which delayed or canceled more than 14,500 commercial flights—was caused by a routine contractor software and hardware upgrade to a legacy telecommunications network managed by defense contractor L3Harris Technologies, compounded by degraded copper wiring at a switching facility. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford emphasized that forensic audits found 'zero evidence of anything AI-related' or foreign cyber intrusion behind the outage.

Records reviewed by the New York Times showed that FAA traffic managers granted emergency exemptions to dozens of long-haul international departures during the four-hour domestic freeze to prevent cascading global crew timeouts, and the agency projected US airline schedules would fully normalize by Sunday (AP News).
sections.whyItMatters: Tracing a nationwide aviation standstill to faulty copper wiring during an L3Harris telecom upgrade highlights the brittle physical infrastructure underlying US air traffic control.

sections.heading: Elon Musk and 115,000 Sign Petition to Reinstate Ousted Chip Chief as WSJ Details Southeast Asian Supply Backdoor
sections.body:
TechCrunch, Wall Street Journal, and Bloomberg — More than 115,000 people, led by Elon Musk and prominent Silicon Valley founders, signed an online petition Saturday demanding that Nvidia's board of directors reverse Friday's ouster of co-founder Jensen Huang. The campaign came as TechCrunch revealed that the chipmaker's chief security officer had quietly left the company in August—months before the counterintelligence probe into Huang's relationship with Singapore-based Megaspeed executive Alice Huang became public—and as Asian governments moved to audit local data-center GPU delivery commitments.

Meanwhile, new investigations by the Wall Street Journal detailed how Huang had constructed a Southeast Asian cloud-rental and subsidiary supply route that kept Chinese AI laboratories supplied with advanced accelerators despite US export controls, reported that Huang had privately belittled newly appointed interim CEO Colette Kress prior to his departure, and profiled a 31-year-old hedge fund trader who reaped massive gains shorting the stock after mapping its China exposure. Bloomberg noted that the resulting sell-off in US AI hardware equities is driving global institutional investors to rotate capital into Indian equities.
sections.whyItMatters: Revelations of an August security-chief exit and a Southeast Asian GPU routing channel deepen Nvidia's regulatory exposure ahead of congressional testimony even as Silicon Valley figures rally behind Huang.

sections.heading: Tesla Opens $299/Month Cybercab Pre-Orders, Chinese AI Labs Curb Open-Weight Cyber Tools, and GTA VI Hits $600M in Pre-Orders
sections.body:
TechCrunch, South China Morning Post, and Le Monde — Tesla opened consumer pre-orders on Saturday for its two-seat autonomous Cybercab 'for personal use,' subject to municipal regulatory geofencing and a mandatory $299 monthly autonomous-driving software subscription fee that CEO Elon Musk acknowledged on social media is currently 'too high' (TechCrunch). Separately, TechCrunch examined a growing 'AI product graveyard' spanning Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri overhaul and OpenAI's troubled consumer super-app push while reviewing multi-screen software tricks for Apple's newly released foldable iPhone Duo.

In East Asia, leading Chinese artificial intelligence laboratories began stripping offensive cybersecurity and exploit-generation capabilities from their open-weight frontier models after state regulators flagged domestic hacking incidents (South China Morning Post), while Chinese platforms purged AI-generated 'blue alien' medical influencers and fabricated historical videos and South Korean police opened a criminal probe into the nation's top-scoring tax-accountant exam candidate after he confessed to cheating with AI glasses (SCMP). In digital entertainment and crypto markets, Le Monde reported that Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI has already generated $600 million in pre-orders ahead of its November 19 launch, while Bitcoin fell to a three-month low on heavy derivatives liquidations (Bloomberg).
sections.whyItMatters: From Tesla's $299 monthly geofenced Cybercab subscription to Chinese labs restricting open-weight cyber tools, AI commercialization is running into pricing and safety boundaries.

sections.heading: UK Parliament Blasts Big Tech Over Online Safety Filters, Open-Source Rivals Target Microsoft School Fees, and AI Spots Cardiac Risk
sections.body:
The Register, Science Daily, and Wall Street Journal — Online child-safety researchers testified before the UK Parliament's Communications and Digital Committee that major social media and generative AI platforms are doing the 'bare minimum' to comply with the Online Safety Act, demonstrating that automated moderation filters can still be bypassed using simple thesaurus word substitutions (The Register). In enterprise software, European open-source productivity vendors Collabora and Nextcloud launched migration campaigns targeting schools and universities after Microsoft introduced per-user fees for previously free educational email and storage accounts (The Register).

In biomedical computing, cardiology researchers reported in Science Daily that deep-learning algorithms detected a previously invisible electrical and structural warning signature in routine heart scans capable of predicting sudden cardiac arrest years in advance, Johns Hopkins neuroscientists identified brain-region volume loss occurring up to a decade before clinical Alzheimer's symptoms appear (Science Daily), and the Wall Street Journal documented how rare-disease patients are using frontier reasoning models to diagnose decades-old medical mysteries.
sections.whyItMatters: While consumer social platforms struggle with basic content filtering and software fee hikes alienate European schools, clinical AI diagnostics are delivering concrete breakthroughs in cardiology and neurology.

bottomLine: Saturday's technology news underscored both the triumphs of physical aerospace engineering and the governance fractures inside the AI and infrastructure economy: SpaceX's first launch-tower catch of a returning orbital Starship spacecraft proved full orbital reusability is within reach, while the L3Harris copper-wiring fault behind the FAA's nationwide flight freeze and the widening counterintelligence disclosures surrounding Nvidia's Southeast Asian chip pipeline exposed how fragile critical US digital and hardware supply chains remain.
